title: A Smile for the House
premise: When Astrid Oyelaran returns to his grandmother's house to bury his twin brother Aden, he discovers the funeral was held for the wrong twin — and that every photograph in the house now shows an extra chair, occupied by a smiling man no one remembers. The house is a ledger of an old debt: in 1974, Astrid's grandmother and her neighbors took something from a dying man, and the house has been holding it in trust ever since. As the last surviving resident of that summer prepares to sign the property over to developers — which would erase the debt's only witness — Astrid must uncover what was taken, return it, and decide whether he is the brother who lived or the one who should have died. In the end, Astrid gives back what was stolen, signs himself into the house as its final resident, and lets the true memory of both twins survive in place of the lie.
about_author: Wendell Brightwater is the pen name of a former probate clerk from coastal Maine who spent eleven years cataloguing unclaimed estates before turning to fiction. His work explores houses as witnesses, and the quiet violence of paperwork.

chapters.title: The Wrong Twin
chapters.summary: Astrid arrives at grandma's house for Aden's funeral and finds the casket already closed, the death certificate bearing his own name. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as he realizes the paperwork has decided which twin survived.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three Chairs
chapters.summary: Sorting photographs for the memorial slideshow, Astrid counts chairs in a 1985 family portrait: twenty-three, though only twenty-two people ever lived there. The extra chair is empty in old prints; in yesterday's photos, someone sits in it. POV: Astrid. Beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Astrid visits Mrs. Okonkwo, the last living neighbor from 1974, who mistakes him for Aden and begs him not to let 'the smiling man' finish the paperwork. Her lawyer confirms she's signing the house away Friday. POV: Astrid. Beat: first hint of the deadline.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Back at the house, Astrid keeps every light burning and counts doors each night — eleven at dusk, twelve by morning. A new door has appeared where the pantry wall used to be. POV: Astrid. Beat: the house begins negotiating.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: In a locked cedar chest, Astrid finds a 1974 ledger book in grandma's handwriting: names, dates, and a column labeled simply OWED, with one entry never crossed out. POV: Astrid, with interleaved ledger excerpts. Beat: guilt inherited like furniture.

chapters.title: The Smiling Man
chapters.summary: The extra chair's occupant appears at the kitchen table, patient and courteous, introducing himself as the estate's executor. He offers Astrid a pen and a simple choice: sign, and forget. POV: Astrid. Beat: terror dressed as politeness.

chapters.title: Aden's Room
chapters.summary: Grieving properly for the first time, Astrid sleeps in Aden's childhood room and dreams his brother's memories — including a summer day in 1974 he couldn't know. POV: Astrid (dream). Beat: grief becoming investigation.

chapters.title: Summer of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, 1974: five neighbors find a migrant worker dying on the road and take his satchel of savings, telling themselves he wouldn't need it. POV: young Grandma Ruth. Beat: the original sin, rendered without excuse.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okonkwo's Confession
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Mrs. Okonkwo with the ledger; she admits her share and reveals the satchel was buried under the house's foundation stones — or so they believed. POV: Astrid. Beat: pity tangled with anger.

chapters.title: Twelve Doors
chapters.summary: The twelfth door opens onto a hallway that shouldn't fit, lined with framed photographs of every resident who ever owed something. Astrid finds his own portrait, already hung. POV: Astrid. Beat: the house knows him.

chapters.title: The Executor's Terms
chapters.summary: The smiling man explains the rules: the debt transfers to whoever holds the memory. If Mrs. Okonkwo signs, the house forgets, and the debt falls to the bloodline — to Astrid. POV: Astrid. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Digging
chapters.summary: Astrid tears up the foundation bed at night and finds a rotted satchel — empty except for a photograph of the dead man, smiling, seated in a chair. POV: Astrid. Beat: hope curdling; the money isn't what was taken.

chapters.title: His Name Was Emeka
chapters.summary: Researching the photograph, Astrid learns the victim's name and traces a daughter, now in her sixties, who was told her father abandoned her. POV: Astrid. Beat: justice outside the law takes human shape.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: Astrid meets Grace, Emeka's daughter, and cannot bring himself to confess; instead he asks about her father and hears the memory the house has been starving for. POV: Astrid. Beat: tenderness as dread.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: The smiling man clarifies: the money was spent long ago; what the house holds is Emeka's name — erased from every record, every memory but the house's. Returning it means remembering him publicly. POV: Astrid. Beat: theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okonkwo signs the papers; the house shudders, doors multiplying overnight, and Astrid wakes to find his own reflection missing from mirrors. POV: Astrid. Beat: lowest point — the debt is his now.

chapters.title: The Chair Waits
chapters.summary: The smiling man sets a second chair beside his own and invites Astrid to sit, promising rest, forgetting, an end to counting doors. Astrid nearly does. POV: Astrid. Beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Astrid files to restore Emeka's name to the county record, tells Grace the truth, and pays her from the estate — justice done outside any court, at real cost to his inheritance and reputation. POV: Astrid. Beat: costly repair.

chapters.title: The House Remembers
chapters.summary: With the name restored, the hallway of portraits rearranges: Emeka's frame moves from the owed-wall to the honored-wall, and the extra chair in the photographs stands empty again. POV: Astrid. Beat: release beginning.

chapters.title: The Last Signature
chapters.summary: The smiling man presents final papers: the house must have a resident of record or collapse into forgetting entirely. Astrid signs — not as heir, but as keeper. POV: Astrid. Beat: chosen burden.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Stone
chapters.summary: Astrid re-carves the headstone to read both twins' names truthfully, and buries the ledger beneath it, closing the account. The twelfth door seals. POV: Astrid. Beat: mourning completed honestly.

chapters.title: A Smile for the House
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Astrid lives on as the house's final resident, lights on, doors counted — eleven, always eleven now. In the newest photograph, two brothers sit side by side, and the house, finally, smiles back. POV: Astrid. Beat: peace earned, vigil accepted.
